page_01: The Perseverance rover landed on Mars in 2021 to look for signs of life.
page_02: The Ingenuity helicopter was the first to fly on another planet!
page_03: The first robot rover drove on the Moon in 1970.
page_04: The space station's robot arm can move cargo heavier than a bus!
page_05: Robot vacuums use sensors so they don't fall down the stairs.
page_06: Many robot lawn mowers stay inside a wire hidden around the lawn.
page_07: Factory robot arms can build cars all day and all night.
page_08: Some robot dogs can climb stairs and even open doors!
page_09: Underwater robots explore the deep sea where people can't go.
page_10: A robot has explored the deepest place in the whole ocean.
page_11: Farm robots can pick strawberries and pull out weeds.
page_12: Milking robots let cows choose when they want to be milked!
page_13: Small delivery robots roll along the sidewalk to bring parcels.
page_14: Warehouse robots carry whole shelves of boxes to the workers.
page_15: Doctors use robot arms to do tiny, careful operations.
page_16: Firefighting robots spray water where it is too hot for people.
page_17: Snake-like rescue robots wriggle through rocks to find people.
page_18: Some robots clean solar panels in the desert without any water.
page_19: Pool robots climb up the walls to scrub them clean.
page_20: A humanoid robot is shaped like a person, with a head, arms and legs.
page_21: Some two-legged robots can run, jump and even do backflips!
page_22: Robot hands use sensors to feel how hard they squeeze, even an egg.
page_23: Some kitchen robots can flip burgers and make pizza.
page_24: A robot is a machine that can sense, think and act by itself.
page_25: Robots have played the piano, the drums and even the trumpet!
page_26: Some robots can paint pictures with a real paint brush.
page_27: Robot pets can wag and wiggle when you pat them.
page_28: The word robot comes from a Czech word that means hard work.
page_29: Kids all over the world build and code robots at school.
page_30: Simple robots can follow a black line using light sensors.
page_31: Many outdoor robots run on sunshine using solar panels.
page_32: Robot vacuums drive back to their dock when they need charging.
page_33: Some tractors can drive themselves across a huge farm field.
page_34: Drones are flying robots that can take photos from the sky.
page_35: Giant robot trucks with no driver carry rocks at Australian mines.
page_36: A reef robot helps protect the Great Barrier Reef from crown-of-thorns starfish.
page_37: Space robots have docked with old satellites to keep them working.
page_38: The Voyager 1 space probe has flown out past all the planets.
page_39: A robot lander called Philae landed on a comet in 2014.
page_40: Sydney's metro trains drive themselves with no driver on board.
page_41: Hospital robots carry meals and medicine down long corridors.
page_42: Scientists used a robot penguin chick to visit real penguins.
page_43: Robot fish can swim with real fish to help scientists study the sea.
page_44: Scientists have built a flying robot about as small as a bee!
page_45: Recycling robots use cameras to sort bottles from paper.
page_46: A robot solved a puzzle cube in less than one second!
page_47: Every year, robots play soccer at the RoboCup world cup.
page_48: Some museums have robot guides that show visitors around.
page_49: Robots need sensors to feel, a computer brain to think and motors to move.
page_50: Thanks for building a world of robot wonders with us!
